subject: Post-demo sanity check: deployment mode and dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@acme-retail.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up after demo — targeting throughput and mode

Thanks for the demo this morning — Ben & Olga. A few follow-ups from our side as we prep an internal feasibility review: 

- We need a clear recommendation on whether to start on Hosted API for speed-to-market vs committing to Dedicated capacity now (our traffic could ramp fast).
- If Dedicated is the right path, would you help us size: target TPS, concurrency per GPU, and recommended GPU family?
- Token mix: our average request is ~450 tokens (prompt + response). Attached is a sample token distribution we exported from our staging logs (prod_token_distribution.csv).

Can you respond with a concise sizing ask that we can pass to our infra and procurement teams? Also looping in Jordan Miles from procurement (procurement@acme-retail.com) for contracting questions.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Li
Head of AI Product — Acme Retail

Attachments: prod_token_distribution.csv (CSV, 28 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — targeting throughput and mode

Hi Emma — great to meet you earlier. Replied inline below and added a proposed mutual action plan at the end so your infra/procurement teams have something executable.

On Hosted vs Dedicated:
- Hosted API: best for immediate launch and unpredictable spikes. Low onboarding overhead and no infra commitment. Good if you want to iterate on prompts and UX quickly.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you expect sustained high sustained TPS (typically >300-500 TPS steady state for production-critical flows) or you need guaranteed latency and isolation. It gives predictable unit costs and reserve GPU pools.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): choose this only if you have strict data residency or regulatory requirements — higher ops lift and longer lead time.

Sizing guidance (initial recommendation):
- Baseline TPS: you mentioned bursts to 1k TPS during promotions and steady-state 200–350 TPS. If that holds, we recommend starting with a small Dedicated pool equivalent to 4 x H100-80GB (or 6 x A100-80GB as a lower-cost alternative) with autoscale headroom.
- Concurrency & per-GPU targets: estimate ~60–90 concurrent streams per H100 for decoder-only models at ~512 context, with continuous batching enabled. For A100 expect ~45–60 concurrent streams depending on quantization/config.
- Token mix consideration: with ~450 tokens/request and a 200–350 TPS steady-state, plan for ~90k–157k tokens/sec. Prefix caching (for shared prompts) can reduce this by up to 20–30% if applicable.

Specific ask for your infra/procurement team: please confirm the following so we can produce a firm Dedicated sizing table and a cost estimate: 
1) Target sustained TPS (avg over 15m window) and 95th percentile burst TPS (numbers you expect during peak campaigns).
2) Typical max response length (tail latency drivers) and whether streaming is required for UX.
3) Top 10 prompts or templates (or share a representative prompt set) — this helps estimate cache hit rates.
4) Any requirement for private VPC or KMS/HSM integration (security).

Attachments: I attached a one-page sizing worksheet to speed this along: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (detailed columns for TPS, token mix, model family, quantization, and desired SLAs).

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- You: send confirmation for items 1–4 above + procurement contact details (we can take DocuSign for SOWs).
- Us: we will return a two-option Dedicated configuration (costed) and a Hosted fallback plan within 48 business hours after we get the numbers.

If you want a quick call with Karthik (he's on cc) to walk through the worksheet, we can slot 30 min tomorrow.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx (Excel, 36 KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@acme-retail.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — targeting throughput and mode

Emma — quick addition from infra sizing side:
- If you prioritize single-digit 95th latency (for short responses), H100 family is our go-to. For cost-sensitive pilots where 95th latency can be in the low double-digits, A100 with INT8/quantized models works well.
- For your ~450-token average, we typically budget ~2.8–3.6 tokens generated per ms on H100 with our optimized kernels (model dependent). Use that to sanity-check token/sec math.
- Default safe starting allocation (fast path): 4 x H100 + 2 x A100 as a mixed pool for burst/queue smoothing — gives both latency headroom and cost optimization.

If you send the token distribution and top prompts (Olga's worksheet helps), we can produce a more granular per-model TPS table.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Li <emma@acme-retail.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up after demo — targeting throughput and mode

Thanks — this is very helpful and actionable. Confirming numbers from our side for the worksheet: 
- Steady-state target: 300 TPS (15m avg)
- 95th percentile burst: 1,100 TPS (short bursts during marketing drives)
- Typical max response length: 600 tokens, streaming preferred for customer chat flows
- Prompt set: shared via attached CSV (we exported top-10 prompts and token stats).

Procurement contact is Jordan Miles (jordan.miles@acme-retail.com) — looping him in. We're comfortable with the mixed-pool approach you suggested; please send the two costed configurations (H100-first and A100-cost-optimized) and a Hosted fallback plan so we can review with infra/procurement.

I've attached the prompt/token CSV and vCard for Jordan: acme_procurement_contact.vcf (2 KB).

Best,
Emma
